fixes.explanation: Nice guess, since gold is what most of us think of when we hear "giving to a king." But David doesn't mention gold or silver anywhere here. He tells the heavenly beings to "…ascribe to the LORD glory and strength." (Psalm 29:1) Glory and strength are what he calls on them to ascribe to Him, and you can't pack those in a cookie box.

Shur is a real wilderness in the Bible (Exodus 15:22), so you know your deserts, and that's not nothing. But David names a different one here: "the LORD shakes the Wilderness of Kadesh." (Psalm 29:8) I know, desert names run together like dough in a hot oven, so mixing them up is no crime, friend.
